description: Cross-language fixture corpus. The TypeScript and Go test suites both read this manifest: valid cases must decode and re-encode to the byte string recorded in canonical.json, and invalid cases must be refused with the recorded reason. A fixture is the only place a protocol example is written down.

valid.name: registration-request
valid.note: The section 4.3 example, with the envelope carrying protocol_version and no connector_id.

valid.name: registration-request-minimal
valid.note: Optional labels absent, capabilities empty, fractional-second timestamp.

valid.name: registration-request-unicode
valid.note: Exercises string escaping parity: quotes, backslash, HTML-significant characters, non-ASCII and an astral-plane character.

valid.name: registration-response
valid.note: Connector identity, signed identity, endpoints and policy digest.

valid.name: heartbeat
valid.note: The section 8 example, including the optional resource summary.

valid.name: heartbeat-minimal
valid.note: Resource reporting omitted, degraded status, zero counters.

valid.name: heartbeat-exponential-load
valid.note: Load small enough to force exponential number formatting, where Go and ECMAScript disagree unless the canonical encoder pins the format.

valid.name: route-publish-opaque-identifiers
valid.note: Identifiers without the conventional prefixes are accepted: docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3 requires consumers to treat identifiers as opaque.

valid.name: route-publish-ack-rejected
valid.note: Rejection carries a stable error class and no free text.

valid.name: data-stream-header
valid.note: The section 12 header fields. It carries no host or port: the connector opens only the destination already bound to route_id.

valid.name: reconnect-request
valid.note: The section 17 reconnect payload with all six fields populated as Stage 0 sends them: version, capabilities, active routes, active streams, and the empty agent-session and workspace-head collections.

valid.name: reconnect-request-after-restart
valid.note: A connector that has just restarted holds nothing. Every collection is empty and every field is still present, which is what lets the control plane restore routes the connector no longer knows about.

valid.name: reconnect-response
valid.note: The authoritative desired state: one route continued with its publication restated, one closed as unknown, and one session re-established.

valid.name: reconnect-response-upgrade-required
valid.note: The section 19 upgrade-required classification, which the connector reports and stops on rather than retrying.

valid.name: data-stream-header-upgrade
valid.note: The section 13.3 upgraded stream: stream_mode selects the idle window the connector applies, and still carries no host or port. Its deadline is the route's expiry, not one exchange's.

invalid.name: unknown-protocol-version
invalid.note: An unknown version is refused, never best-effort parsed.

invalid.name: unknown-message-type
invalid.note: An unknown type is rejected rather than ignored, so no service can be talked into a command the schema never defined.

invalid.name: trailing-data
invalid.note: A second value smuggled after the first must not be silently ignored.

invalid.name: oversized-malformed-frame
invalid.note: Oversized and malformed at once. The reason must be the byte bound, which proves the bound is applied to the raw bytes before deserialisation.

invalid.name: registration-request-oversized-payload
invalid.note: Every field satisfies its own bound, yet the payload exceeds the bound declared for its message type.

invalid.name: heartbeat-unknown-property
invalid.note: additionalProperties is false throughout, which is what stops sensitive process detail riding along in a resource summary (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 8).

invalid.name: registration-request-with-connector-id
invalid.note: The registration exchange precedes identity assignment.

invalid.name: heartbeat-without-connector-id
invalid.note: Every post-enrolment message is attributed to a connector identity.

invalid.name: registration-response-insecure-endpoint
invalid.note: A plaintext ws:// endpoint cannot be assigned to a connector.

invalid.name: route-publish-no-allowed-sessions
invalid.note: A published route always names the browser sessions authorised to use it.

invalid.name: bad-timestamp
invalid.note: Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC; an offset form is refused.

invalid.name: data-stream-header-with-destination
invalid.note: The browser side cannot smuggle a destination host or port into the stream header (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 12, docs/SECURITY.md section 9).

invalid.name: reconnect-request-missing-workspace-head-state
invalid.note: All six section 17 fields are required. An omitted collection is a refused frame, not an empty one, so a connector cannot quietly stop reporting a category.

invalid.name: reconnect-request-workspace-head-with-source
invalid.note: Workspace head state describes the repository, never its contents (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 9). additionalProperties is false, so source cannot ride along.

invalid.name: reconnect-response-continue-without-route
invalid.note: A continued route must restate its publication, otherwise a connector that lost its route table could not resume the route it is being told to keep.

invalid.name: reconnect-response-revoke-with-route
invalid.note: A revoked route carries no publication. Carrying one would make a closure look like a grant.

invalid.name: data-stream-header-unknown-mode
invalid.note: stream_mode is a closed set. A mode this version does not define is refused rather than treated as request_response, so a future framing cannot be silently downgraded into one this connector would relay on different terms.
